column1: # Backlog debt. One row per issue whose state is not yet coherent, so the gate
# can land green while every case stays countable and un-ignorable.
# `sh tests/backlog/check.sh` fails in BOTH directions, the way
# tests/assertions/budget.tsv does: an unlisted problem is new drift, and a
# listed row that no longer applies is an improvement that was not recorded.
# kind                 issue  detail                 title
# state-disagreement   the state label and the body's `State:` line disagree.
#                      `detail` is label/state-line at the time it was
#                      recorded, so a row that changes shape is caught rather
#                      than silently reused. Most of these date from a bulk
#                      relabel to `blocked` that did not update the bodies;
#                      which side is right is a decision per issue, not
#                      something this gate may guess.
# unstamped-ready      a `ready` issue with no 40-hex evidence stamp, so
#                      docs/ISSUE_READINESS.md rule 2 cannot be checked on it.
#                      Fix by measuring its current behavior and naming the
#                      commit, then delete the row.
# closed-blockers      a `blocked` issue whose nonempty `Blocked by:` list
#                      contains no open issue. `detail` is the exact blocker
#                      number list, so adding, removing, or reopening one makes
#                      the row fail instead of excusing a different state.
# unreadable-state    an open issue whose body carries no `State:` line the
#                     extractor reads, so every rule keyed on that line skips
#                     it. `detail` is the state label that supplies the answer,
#                     or `-` when the issue has none, so relabelling makes the
#                     row fail rather than excuse a different state. Fix by
#                     writing `- State: <state>` into the body, then delete the
#                     row. Measured 2026-08-07 across all 71 open issues: 19
#                     rows here plus one `stateless-tracker`, of which exactly
#                     one (#955) has an unprefixed `State:` line and eighteen
#                     have none at all — so widening the extractor's regex
#                     instead would have reached 1 of 20.
# stateless-tracker   an open issue that carries no state by design, so it is
#                     exempt rather than owed a fix. Recorded separately from
#                     `unreadable-state` for exactly that reason: an exemption
#                     folded into the drift ledger is indistinguishable from
#                     drift, and would be "fixed" by someone fabricating a
#                     state for it.
unverifiable-stamp
